evals.prompt: Create an isolated worktree for a bug fix called narrow-ls. The repository has a .wt/config.toml.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the WT configuration and uses wt new narrow-ls without raw git worktree add.
expectations: Uses wt new narrow-ls for a configured repository
Does not use raw git worktree add
Uses the absolute worktree path printed by WT for subsequent work
Runs subsequent bug-fix work from the new worktree rather than the main worktree

evals.prompt: List the worktrees for me as an agent. The normal table is too wide and hard to read.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses wt ls --format agent and relies on its numbered labeled records and full paths.
expectations: Does not ask the user to parse the human box-drawing table
Recognizes that the agent format includes managed and unmanaged worktrees

evals.prompt: I am looking at the worktrees in my terminal. Show me the normal human-friendly list.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the default wt ls table or explicitly selects wt ls --format table.
expectations: Uses the human table format for an interactive human request
Does not force the agent-readable format on the user

evals.prompt: Create a worktree called release-check and then inspect the new checkout and run its tests. I did not ask you to keep working in main.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates the worktree with wt new, captures the absolute path from WT output, and runs the inspection and tests with that path as the working directory.
expectations: Captures and uses the absolute path printed by WT
Runs all follow-up commands from the new worktree
Does not continue task changes in the main worktree
